sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: Moves beyond uni-dimensional income poverty to capture overlapping deprivations experienced by individuals simultaneously in **health, education, and living standards**.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: Utilizes the **Alkire-Foster (AF) methodology**, a globally recognized mathematical method for measuring multidimensional poverty developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and UNDP.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: Employs **Headcount Ratio (H)**—the proportion of people who are multidimensionally poor—and **Intensity of Deprivation (A)**—the average proportion of weighted indicators in which poor people are deprived.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) = H × A**, reflecting both the incidence and intensity of poverty.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Assessed across 111 developing countries by UNDP and OPHI using 10 indicators.
Standardized international comparison of deprivations in health, education, and living standards.
Frequent Prelims questions on partner organizations, indicators, and threshold levels.
Developed by NITI Aayog with technical support from OPHI and UNDP, using 12 indicators.
Aligned with national development goals, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and flagship welfare schemes.
Mains evaluation of poverty alleviation schemes and cooperative federalism (state-wise tracking).
Income poverty tracks monetary shortfall; Multidimensional tracks direct deprivations in basic needs.
Monetary poverty can fluctuate with inflation; multidimensional poverty reflects structural deprivations.
Critical analytical distinction for Mains essay and GS Paper III answers on inclusive growth.

items.definition: A flexible technique for counting multidimensional poverty that identifies the poor by considering the number of deprivations they suffer simultaneously.
The threshold below which a person is considered deprived in a specific indicator (e.g., lacking access to improved sanitation or cooking fuel).
The proportion of weighted indicators in which a person must be deprived to be classified as multidimensionally poor (typically set at k=33% or 1/3rd of weighted deprivations).
NITI Aayog National MPI Reports, NFHS (National Family Health Survey) data source, Tendulkar and Rangarajan committees (monetary counterparts).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Region / Zone Details**: Highest concentration of multidimensional poverty is observed in central and eastern Indian states such as Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.
• **Driving Advantages**: Rapid declines recorded in states focusing on targeted governance, rural infrastructure, financial inclusion, and piped water delivery.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Inter-state disparities, nutritional deficiencies (anaemia/stunting), quality of learning outcomes, and clean cooking fuel access.
• **Policy Interventions**: PM Ujjwala Yojana, PM Poshan, Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, and direct benefit transfers (DBT).

items.title: Mnemonic for National MPI Pillars
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: H.E.L.P. (Health, Education, Living Standards Pledged)
• **Decoded Meaning**: The 3 core dimensions of the National MPI: Health, Education, and Living Standards.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly verifies if a proposed indicator falls within the 3 core dimensions or acts as a distractor.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember **12-3-33** for National MPI: 12 indicators, 3 dimensions, and 33.3% poverty cutoff threshold.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that income poverty and multidimensional poverty yield identical headcount ratios. This is false; deprivation overlap means people above the income poverty line can still suffer multidimensional deprivations.

Mains Value Addition: Quote Amartya Sen's capability approach ('Poverty is not merely lack of income, but failure of basic capabilities') to elevate your GS-3 answers on inclusive growth and human development.

keyTakeaways: Multidimensional poverty captures simultaneous deprivations across health, education, and living standards using the Alkire-Foster methodology.
India's National MPI by NITI Aayog tracks 12 indicators across 3 dimensions, enabling granular district-level policy targeting.
Bridging regional disparities requires a convergence of flagship welfare interventions like Jal Jeevan Mission, Ujjwala, and Ayushman Bharat.
